extracted.intended_audience: NIH study section members, clinical epidemiologists, pediatric infectious disease and metabolomics researchers preparing/analyzing a K01 grant study
extracted.subtask_description: Design and analysis plan for an NIH K01-sponsored metabolomics study to evaluate urine metabolite profiles in pediatric community-acquired pneumonia, including sample-size/power, classification, statistical methods, missing-data rules, and training/mentorship plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple testing correction (false discovery rate)
rubrics_metrics.description: To account for multiple testing which arises due to metabolites from the same child we will use false discovery rate procedures, such as Benjamini-Hochberg procedure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrate distribution of variance components and ICCs among metabolites and describe proportion associated with age/sex by the FDR procedure; Benjamini-Hochberg cited as the chosen procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imputation rule for missing metabolite concentrations
rubrics_metrics.description: Impute the missing concentration of the metabolite if it has between 10-30% missing in the dataset.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is implemented as a subanalysis when certain metabolites are unable to be quantified accurately (7 of 50 had random missing patterns in preliminary data). References provided (53,54).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pathogen classification definitions (viral, bacterial, co-infection, unknown)
rubrics_metrics.description: Viral Etiology: NP swab positive for virus AND NP swab negative for bacteria AND negative cultures. Bacterial Etiology: NP swab negative for virus AND blood/pleural fluid culture positive for bacteria OR NP swab positive for bacteria AND procalcitonin (PCT) ≥ 1.5 ng/mL. Viral/Bacterial Co-Infection: viral classification AND bacterial criteria met. Unknown: NP swab negative for virus and bacteria AND culture negative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table 4 enumerates included pathogens (viruses: influenza, parainfluenza, RSV, human metapneumovirus, enterovirus/rhinovirus, adenovirus, coronavirus, bocavirus; bacteria: S. pneumoniae, M. pneumoniae, C. pneumoniae, Legionella; culture positives include S. pneumoniae, H. influenzae, S. aureus, S. pyogenes, Klebsiella). Use of multiple molecular and microbiological tests is emphasized to increase accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Molecular and microbiological testing requirements for pathogen detection
rubrics_metrics.description: Perform PCR to detect pneumococcal autolysin A (lytA) and pneumococcal surface adhesion (psaA) on all NP swabs; consider present/absent. Blood or pleural culture positivity classifies pneumococcus as positive. A subset classified as unknown will be further analyzed using 16S rRNA on blood to identify bacteria at genus level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: lytA/psaA may be discordant; plan for additional analytic handling (see latent class modelling). Multiple tests together improve etiologic classification because conventional cultures are insensitive in children.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of PCA and PLS-DA for multivariate metabolomics
rubrics_metrics.description: First stage: perform PCA and PLS-DA to reduce correlated metabolite data into uncorrelated components and visualize inherent clusters; use PCA results to guide number of latent variables or PLS components for PLS-DA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PCA/PLS-DA allow visual scores plots and loading plots; PLS-DA optimizes separation between groups and handles multicollinearity and noisy metabolomics data. From PLS-DA obtain VIP scores and regression coefficients to identify important variables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of important metabolites via VIP scores and fold differences
rubrics_metrics.description: Use variable importance in projection (VIP) score from PLS-DA and large fold differences in metabolite concentrations to identify potentially important metabolites separating groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Visualizations such as score plots and radar plots (2-fold circles) support interpretation; overlapping vs. non-overlapping metabolites may indicate infection vs pathogen-specific signatures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analysis of individual metabolites using ANCOVA with covariate selection rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Use analysis of covariance (ANCOVA) to compare groups with respect to individual metabolite concentrations including clinical and demographic covariates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covariates with a p-value < .10 in 1-to-1 regressions will be considered statistically significant and examined in the final model. Final model evaluates means differences via t-contrasts; t-statistic from each contrast used to compare groups. Account for multiple testing using FDR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exploratory pathway/network analysis using Metscape
rubrics_metrics.description: As an exploratory analysis, conduct pathway analysis via Metscape to construct metabolic networks using differentiating metabolites to aid interpretation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use network construction to contextualize identified metabolites within metabolic pathways; cited reference (70).

rubrics_metrics.name: Linear mixed models for longitudinal metabolite analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: For longitudinal changes, use a linear mixed model with normalized metabolite concentration as dependent variable, a between-subject variable (group: viral, bacterial, healthy), and a within-individual variable (time: baseline, 24 hours, 14 days) plus covariates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary goal: assess overall group effects and group-by-time interactions. Group differences over time tested using least square means contrasts. Transform concentrations if necessary to approximate normality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling time-varying therapies as covariates
rubrics_metrics.description: Include time-varying covariates for each therapy (e.g., bronchodilators) administered within sampling timeframe to evaluate their influence on temporal changes in metabolite profiles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This helps disentangle therapy effects from infection-response signals in longitudinal analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rules for inclusion based on sample timepoints and subanalyses for incomplete data
rubrics_metrics.description: Urine samples from cases and controls who provide samples at 3 time points will be eligible; if only two time points are received from cases or controls, perform a subanalysis including these samples with the cohort having all 3 time points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim-specific eligibility: Aim 1 and 3 rely on 3 timepoints; power calculations assume data availability at all scheduled timepoints but include planned subanalyses for partial data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample-size and power calculation assumptions and thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: Power analyses performed assuming log-normal distribution where difference defined as linear t-contrast between logs of geometric means; coefficient of variation (CV) assumed 0.5; significance threshold p<0.01; target 80% power to detect specified geometric mean ratios.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: planned enrollment of 125 healthy controls expecting 110 with ≥3 samples gives 80% power to detect GMR=1.38 in one analysis; enrollment of 250 cases with 175 viral and 125 controls gives 80% power to detect GMR=1.21. For longitudinal Aim 4, 50 cases and 50 matched controls (all 3 timepoints) give 80% power to detect GMR=1.61 with alpha=0.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Latent Class Modeling when no gold standard exists
rubrics_metrics.description: If lytA and psaA results are discordant for detecting S. pneumoniae (no perfect gold standard), use Latent Class Modeling (LCM) to estimate probability of pneumococcal infection, including culture-positive blood/pleural cases as known disease cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement LCM using Mplus 7.1; this approach handles imperfect tests by estimating latent disease status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data transformation to achieve normality
rubrics_metrics.description: Continuous variables (metabolite concentrations) will be transformed if necessary to achieve a normal distribution prior to parametric analyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transformations (e.g., log) are applied consistently with power analysis assumptions (log-normal) and t-contrast framework.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of technical replicates and multi-site assay validation
rubrics_metrics.description: In Year 1, technical replicates (n=50) will be assayed at two sites to validate NMR spectral acquisition and inter-site consistency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: N’s in timeline include three timepoints per sample; multi-site replication supports assay reliability and reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expected metabolite detection per sample
rubrics_metrics.description: Anticipate identification and quantification of approximately 50-60 metabolites in each urine sample.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This expectation is based on preliminary NMR results and cited literature (12,72) and informs downstream multiple-testing considerations and power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical significance threshold for analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt a conservative alpha (p) threshold of 0.01 for power calculations and detection of geometric mean ratios.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use FDR for multiple testing control in conjunction with chosen alpha for power planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification and interpretation of overlapping vs. non-overlapping metabolites
rubrics_metrics.description: Interpret metabolites found in both bacterial vs healthy and viral vs healthy analyses as potential general infection indicators; non-overlapping metabolites (e.g., taurine vs betaine) may indicate bacterial versus viral pathogens specifically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use combined analyses and biological plausibility to prioritize metabolites for targeted validation (LC/MS) and translation to point-of-care tests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of 16S rRNA for unresolved/unknown classifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Samples classified as 'unknown' will be further analyzed using 16S rRNA on blood samples to identify bacteria at the genus level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This molecular approach aims to reduce unknown etiologies when cultures and NP swabs are negative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsible Conduct of Research (RCR) and ethics training requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain current CITI training; attend seminars/workshops (University of Cincinnati CCTST seminars, Human Subjects Protection symposium every 2 years), formal coursework (e.g., Ethics in Research/Scientific Integrity), and metabolomics workshops with sessions on -omics ethics and data management.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training topics include IRB regulations, informed consent, research with protected populations, data sharing, ethical failures, roles/responsibilities, data retention and reporting; attendance and completion tracked; aligns with NIH RCR Notice #NOT-OD-10-1019.

rubrics_metrics.name: IRB and institutional SOP compliance and protocol management
rubrics_metrics.description: Use CCHMC IRB Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) on obtaining informed consent, documentation procedures, participant recruitment and protection; IRB assigns research compliance specialists to divisions to facilitate protocol development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review SOPs with mentors and utilize as relevant; all research reviewed by co-mentors, division scientific review, and IRB to confirm scientific validity and responsible conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mentorship, oversight, and career development commitments
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary mentor will meet weekly then bi-weekly (years 3–5), provide protected research time (≥75%), assist with manuscript/grant development, set goals (2–4 publications per year), conduct quarterly advisory committee meetings, and provide evaluations for annual NIH progress reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mentoring includes access (adjacent offices, open door), shared oversight with co-mentors, and institutional processes for annual faculty evaluation; mentors will also support protected effort and some professional fees for K award needs.
